newsitem.title: USA: Phelps Dodge moves back Norwich shutdown.
newsitem.headline: Phelps Dodge moves back Norwich shutdown.

text.p: Phelps Dodge Corp moved its maintanence shutdown of its Norwich, Conn., continuous cast copper rod mill back two weeks, sources familiar with the situation said.
Originally scheduled for the last two weeks in August, the shutdown is now planned for the first two weeks in September, sources said.
A Phelps Dodge spokesman told Reuters that "scheduling issues" accounted for the change.
Asked if copper demand accounted for any part of the decision, the spokesman said, "Yes, but it was only part of the decision." He declined to be more specific.
"It probably means that demand is either spectacular or they're waiting on parts for maintanence," said one Phelps Dodge customer.
"Phelps Dodge rarely makes such decision based on commercial factors," said one source familiar with the situation. "It's probably an issue with (mechanical) parts."
Copper rod is used to make wire and cable, which accounts for roughly 60 percent of primary copper demand.
Wire demand is currently the one strong sector of U.S. copper demand, with other demand sectors languishing in the summer doldrums, sources said.
(Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
